Advisory note: BVI (as a British Overseas Territory) is not an automatic beneficiary of UK tax treaty coverage; BVI relies on its own network of Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) and limited extended-territory provisions.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: UK national statutes: (1) The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/692, as amended by SI 2019/1511 and SI 2020/961); (2) The Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018; (3) The Proceeds of Crime Act 2002; (4) The Terrorism Act 2000 (as amended); (5) The Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022, Part 1 (UK Register of Overseas Entities); (6) Companies Act 2006, Part 21A, and the Register of People with Significant Control Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/341). BVI constituent-territory instruments: (1) BVI Business Companies Act 2004 (as amended); (2) BVI Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System Act 2017 (BOSSS); (3) BVI Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Code of Practice 2022; (4) BVI Financial Services Commission Act 2001.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (V.I. Registry)
Notary Public (England and Wales) or BVI Notary/Commissioner of Oaths

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Proof of Residential Address (Utility Bill or Bank Statement, issued within last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or deposit-taking bank; notarized by a Notary Public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: BVI UBO Declaration and Registered Agent Onboarding Packet
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: BVI licensed Registered Agent (AML compliance file)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against: (1) UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) consolidated sanctions list; (2) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (3) US OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists; (4) BVI Financial Services Commission published sanctions and enforcement notices; (5) EU Consolidated Sanctions List (defensive/reputational); (6) global PEP databases (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones, Refinitiv), with enhanced due diligence (EDD) for PEPs per FATF Recommendation 12 and UK MLR 2017 regulation 33; and (7) adverse-media and negative-news checks. All natural persons at or above the 25% UBO threshold must be cleared prior to incorporation filing and again prior to Stripe/Shopify Payments merchant underwriting.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (V.I. Registry) — electronic name check and reservation via a BVI-licensed Registered Agent using the VIRRGIN online system; for any UK trading-name or overseas-entity registration: UK Companies House GOV.UK e-filing portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: BVI Business Companies Act 2004 s.6: the name of a BVI Business Company must be in Latin-script characters (standard English alphabet), may include Arabic numerals, and must end with a corporate designator: 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Corp', 'Incorporated', 'Inc', 'Société Anonyme' or 'S.A.'. Foreign-script names are not permitted. UK Companies House (trading name or overseas entity registration): names must use the permitted Companies House character set and be transliterated into standard English characters; the name must not be the 'same as' an existing name on the Companies House index.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: BVI: upon rejection, the applicant (through its BVI-licensed Registered Agent) may re-file a modified or fresh name with the BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs; the agent may request reconsideration within 10 business days of the rejection notice; if reconsideration fails, an appeal may be made to the BVI Financial Services Commission and thereafter to the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (Commercial Division). A BVI name reservation is extendable by fresh re-application filed before the reservation window lapses. UK (Companies House): within 28 days of a name-rejection notice, the applicant may file an administrative review with Companies House; upon refusal, an appeal lies to the High Court under ss.67–73 of the Companies Act 2006; UK name reservations are non-extendable and require a fresh application after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for BVI statutory purposes only: the BVI BC must maintain a registered office at the BVI-licensed Registered Agent's address; virtual/home offices cannot serve as the statutory registered office. For UK online-retail operations (ISIC 4791), a UK virtual office or serviced/co-working address is generally acceptable to Companies House, HMRC, Stripe, and Shopify Payments, provided it is a genuine monitored business address and the merchant can evidence business activity upon request; a hybrid arrangement (BVI agent office + UK serviced address) is recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 10% probability of unannounced inspection within the first 12 months of operation, increasing to approximately 25% cumulative probability within 24 months if the BVI BC registers for UK VAT/EORI and routes high card volume through Stripe/Shopify Payments; HMRC and Companies House retain unannounced inspection rights, and the BVI Financial Services Commission may conduct agent-level compliance inspections.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: BVI Government Incorporation Fee (authorized capital up to US$50,000 / 50,000 shares)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory incorporation tariff under the BVI Business Companies Act 2004 (Schedule 1)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: British Virgin Islands Business Companies Act, 2004 (as amended), Part II (Incorporation, ss. 4-10), s. 7 (registered office), s. 8 (registered agent); BVI Business Companies Regulations, 2005 (as amended)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission (FSC); electronic filings submitted via the BVI VIRRGIN online portal through a licensed registered agent
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association submitted with Form B1 (Application for Incorporation) to the BVI Registrar of Corporate Affairs
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; the Company may authorize share capital of 50,000 ordinary shares at USD 1.00 each (or with no par value) and allot shares for such consideration as the Board determines
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription by the incorporator for 100 ordinary shares of USD 1.00 each in the Company is approved, allotted, and issued, and the register of members is updated accordingly. RESOLVED, that the registered office at the office of the licensed registered agent, Road Town, Tortola, British Virgin Islands, is adopted as the statutory registered office under Section 7 of the BVI Business Companies Act, 2004. RESOLVED, that [Director A] and [Director B] are appointed first directors, and [Officer C] is appointed Corporate Secretary, each serving until removed or replaced. RESOLVED, that the directors are authorised to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and take all steps required to commence the online retail business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of BVI-Licensed Registered Agent and Company Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI Financial Services Commission (FSC) — licensed Registered Agents (Approved Persons)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retain a BVI licensed registered agent to act as the statutory registered agent and submit the incorporation application. Instruct the agent to run a name search in the BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs and reserve the proposed corporate name (suffix: Limited, Corporation, Incorporated, Ltd, Corp, Inc or similar). Deliver the full KYC package of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners, and execute the engagement letter with payment of the agent's professional fee.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request submitted by the registered agent
Certified passport copy of each director and shareholder
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, not older than 3 months)
Bank reference letter for each beneficial owner
Curriculum vitae or business resume of proposed directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused as identical or confusingly similar to an existing or reserved name, two alternative names must be submitted within 3 business days. If the Registry queries the KYC package, corrected and certified documents must be re-filed within 5 business days; no monetary penalty applies at this pre-filing stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Incorporation Application and Memorandum & Articles with the Registry of Corporate Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs via the VIRRGIN electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent prepares the English-language Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A), completes Form B1, and e-files both documents on VIRRGIN. The agent simultaneously pays the USD 350 government incorporation fee. The M&A must state the company name, authorised share capital, registered office address, registered agent details, and the objects or statement that the company has unrestricted objects. The application must include consents of the registered agent and the provider of the registered office.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association executed by the incorporator
Consent of the licensed registered agent
Consent of the registered office address provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for correction, the registered agent must respond within 14 days by amending the M&A or correcting Form B1. Failure to cure within 14 days causes rejection, after which a new application with a fresh filing fee is required; timely correction carries no penalty. Rejected filings may be refiled once the stated ground is resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Post-Registration Corporate Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (certificate issuance) and the Company's Board of Directors (post-registration governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The Board then adopts the first written resolutions to allot the subscribed shares, adopt the registered office and registered agent, appoint the first directors and corporate secretary, approve share certificates, and establish the statutory registers (register of members, directors, and charges). The registered agent also files the beneficial ownership particulars with the FSC for the BVI Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) system.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed
First written resolutions of the Board of Directors
Register of members, register of directors, and register of charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains an error (e.g., misspelled name or incorrect date), apply to the Registry for administrative rectification or a Certificate of Amendment of Memorandum and/or Articles. Incomplete statutory registers must be completed immediately because they are public inspection documents; no fine applies for initial preparation but late filing of the register of directors with the registered agent must be cured promptly.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC); official portal: https://www.gov.uk/gov/organisations/hm-revenue-customs and https://www.tax.service.gov.uk/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The BVI Business Company is a foreign incorporated entity. For UK VAT, the entity must register via HMRC's online 'Register for VAT' service (Form VAT1) using Government Gateway, identifying itself as a non-established taxable person where no UK establishment exists. A GB VAT registration number will be issued. For UK corporation tax, a non-UK company with a UK permanent establishment must register with HMRC through the Non-Resident Company procedure to obtain a Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) and file annual CT600 returns. Registration evidence includes certificate of incorporation, foreign tax identification number, and UK agent/place-of-business details where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: UK does not have check-the-box elections. Available statutory elections include: VAT group registration under VATA 1994 s.43 (if a UK establishment exists); election under CTA 2009/10 for associated enterprises concerning UK tax residence and permanent establishment attributions; and hybrid mismatch reporting/elections under CTA 2009 Part 6A where the BVI entity is subject to divergent tax treatment elsewhere.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: £90,000 UK taxable turnover for UK-established businesses; no registration threshold for non-established overseas entities that make any taxable supply in the UK. Distance selling and online marketplace rules may treat the marketplace as liable for overseas sellers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or government-mandated e-invoicing. However, Making Tax Digital (MTD) requires VAT-registered businesses above the threshold to keep digital records and file VAT returns using MTD-compatible software with HMRC APIs. Imported goods require customs declarations via the Customs Declaration Service (CDS) and postponed VAT accounting is available.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from the UK to a destination outside the UK are zero-rated if exported by the supplier or a person acting on their behalf within statutory time limits (generally 3 months from the time of supply) and evidence of export is retained. B2B services supplied to a customer belonging outside the UK are generally outside the scope of UK VAT under place-of-supply rules; services directly connected to exported goods may be zero-rated under VATA 1994 s.30 and SI 1995/2518.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic SAD/C21 via Customs Declaration Service)
Bill of Lading or Airway Waybill showing departure from the UK
Commercial invoice confirming 0% VAT treatment and exporter details
Bank or payment service settlement evidence (e.g., SWIFT or Stripe payout records) proving export proceeds were received
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or careless export zero-rating claims attract HMRC assessments for up to 4 years (20 years in cases of deliberate error), penalties under Finance Act 2007 Sch 24 up to 100% of VAT lost, default surcharge under VATA 1994, and interest. Criminal prosecution under CEMA 1979 s.170 and VATA 1994 s.72 may result in imprisonment, full VAT clawback, and forfeiture of goods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (with HM Treasury as the competent authority for financial sanctions and residual exchange control matters)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United Kingdom operates a fully liberalised capital and current account convertibility regime. There are no general exchange controls, no restriction on foreign-currency accounts, and no statutory authorisation requirement for the repatriation of dividends, profits, or share capital. Convertibility may be impeded only by targeted financial sanctions administered by HM Treasury's Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI), antimony-laundering countermeasures, or where a counterparty bank has independent internal policy restrictions on jurisdictions perceived as tax havens. Profit remittance from a UK bank account of a BVI Business Company is lawful and unregulated provided that the underlying distribution satisfies the BVI Companies Act solvency test and the receiving bank's beneficial ownership and source-of-funds checks are cleared.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds under UK law. Export receipts may be retained, settled, or converted into any currency at the exporter's discretion without obligation to surrender to the Bank of England or HM Revenue & Customs. The only applicable requirements are conventional banking record-keeping, anti-money-laundering reporting for suspicious transactions, sanctions screening, and accurate bookkeeping for corporation tax and VAT purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility, subject to FCA authorisation or registration as an Authorised Electronic Money Institution (AEMI) or Authorised Payment Institution (API). Offshore digital EMIs without a UK establishment can provide merchant accounts and virtual IBANs to BVI companies, but must apply equal KYC/CDD standards and typically require a genuine commercial nexus, summary financial statements, and proof of physical trade. Legal constraints include the loss of EEA passporting into the UK post-Brexit, tougher source-of-funds verification for tax-exempt offshore entities, and OFSI sanctions screening. EMI accounts are operationally viable for low-risk Ecommerce receipts from Stripe and Shopify Payments, but are not yet a mature substitute for a tier-1 clearing bank for high-value international wire settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted by UK banks and regulated EMIs, provided that the director's identity is verified through a live video interview and the BVI company's registers are digitally validated. For tier-1 UK banks, a BVI holding company with a purely non-resident board and no UK nexus may be required to undergo an enhanced due-diligence interview by telephone or video. Physical board attendance is not a blanket statutory mandate, but certain risk committees may request a physical meeting for high-risk BVI structures, particularly where the beneficial owner holds a passport from a sanctioned or high-MLA jurisdiction. A reliable local registered agent, a clean source-of-funds narrative, and a contractual nexus to UK payment rails materially reduce the need for in-person attendance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BVI Business Company has tax-exempt status and no economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, register of directors and shareholders, beneficial ownership declaration, BVI Economic Substance Notification evidence or waiver, board resolution confirming actual management, and either a VAT registration or transactional evidence demonstrating real economic activity in online retailing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign beneficial owner without UK residency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Government-issued passport, proof of residential address, professional reference, source-of-wealth statement, trading licence or local business registration in the beneficial owner's jurisdiction, no adverse sanctions screening result, and an explanation of the commercial rationale for the UK banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity card settlement volume from Stripe and Shopify Payments without a prior UK banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully reconciled sales ledger, audience-specific marketplace reports, refund and chargeback history, customer invoices, KYC files of counterparties, warehouse or fulfilment agreements, and a cash-flow forecast evidencing legitimate e-commerce operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments from jurisdictions considered high-risk by UK financial crime screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoice, bill of lading, customs declaration, courier tracking log, proof of product authenticity for 3D printers and consumables, business emails, due diligence on the foreign buyer, and a written AML risk assessment prepared by an external compliance consultant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The registered office is a BVI service-provider address used by many unrelated companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered agent confirmation of sole-client relationship, physical operational address in the UK or a warehouse/premises lease, utility bill in the company's name, and a detailed corporate structure chart showing the board, officers, and ultimate beneficial owner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection should be executed via SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's personal or corporate bank account to the BVI company's UK mirror or operational account. The payment instruction must include the full legal name of the beneficiary, the BVI company's registered address, the UK bank account IBAN, and a purpose narrative such as 'Capital contribution to BVI Business Company for investment in UK/EU e-commerce operations'. Although the UK does not maintain a codified positive list of purpose codes, the bank may require the remitter to articulate whether the funds are equity capital, shareholder loan, or working capital. A board resolution approving the capital contribution, executed share allotment documents, and a source-of-funds declaration should accompany the first transfer to satisfy AML checks. Payments above EUR 10,000 are automatically screened under the Funds Transfer Regulation and no structuring or split-transaction techniques may be used.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and trade disbursements for the procurement of desktop 3D printers, resin filaments, and consumables should be settled through SWIFT MT103 direct wires for low-value recurring purchases, and through commercial letters of credit (MT700) where a supplier requires documentary payment security. The standard rail is an irrevocable documentary letter of credit opened by a UK or international tier-1 bank in favour of the overseas manufacturer, with invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or airway bills, certificates of origin, and inspection certificates as the required presentation documents. For high-frequency e-commerce inventory replenishment, a bank-open account with supplier factoring or trade credit may be accepted where a proven payment history exists. All disbursements must be processed in a manner consistent with OFSI sanctions screening and must preserve a complete audit trail of purchase orders, supplier due diligence, currency spot-rate confirmations, and actual Swift MT103 or MT700 advise.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (Vanilla FX forwards) with a UK-authorised bank or FCA-regulated payment institution for deterministic inventory-replenishment cycles

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market supplier currencies where convertibility is restricted, such as certain Asian or Middle Eastern currency pairs, provided the BVI company's bank accepts the credit exposure
Cross-Currency Swaps for medium-term shareholder loans or trade finance facilities to manage principal and interest exposure between USD, GBP, EUR, and CNY
FX Spot transactions executed at transparent market rates with spread limits agreed by the treasury policy
Options-based structures such as FX collars and vanilla FX options are permissible, but are not considered necessary for a low-risk hardware e-commerce treasury profile

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Annual Government License Fee (Business Companies Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs / BVI Financial Services Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; payment is due on each annual anniversary with a one-month grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment fee of USD 50 if settled in the second month; USD 250 if settled later; continued non-payment triggers administrative strike-off and subsequent dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Economic Substance Annual Notification / ES Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the financial year end; default financial year end is 31 December unless a different fiscal year is elected
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic fine of USD 400 for late filing; additional fine of USD 500 for false or incomplete declarations; director or officer liability may be imposed for intentional non-compliance; repeated failure may result in strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Annual Return and Registered Agent Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs through the licensed BVI Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not later than nine months after the end of the financial year; applies to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2024
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual return is an offence; the company and every responsible officer may be liable to a fine of up to USD 10,000; continued default may lead to administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit applies to a BVI Business Company carrying on non-regulated online retail activity. Mandatory audit would arise only if the company is a licensed financial services entity, listed on a recognised exchange, required by its memorandum or articles, or ordered by shareholders holding at least 25% of votes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: BVI Business Companies Act (Cap 218) requires accurate financial records to be kept; no statutory obligation to prepare IFRS or Local GAAP financial statements unless an Economic Substance Report is required. IFRS is generally adopted on a voluntary basis for internal management and financing purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the BVI Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) system, the registered agent must receive an annual confirmation of all registrable beneficial owners, including any share transfers giving rise to a change in ownership or control. The agent must file any beneficial ownership change with the Registry within 15 days and update the company's internal BO register immediately. The annual confirmation is submitted as part of the company's annual compliance review; failure to update UBO details may result in fines and imprisonment.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 2,800 per annum for BVI licensed registered agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for a non-regulated e-commerce entity; if audit becomes mandatory due to regulated activity, typical fee is USD 4,000 - USD 9,000 for a small online retail holding company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% UK main Corporation Tax rate (FY2024/25); 19% Small Profits Rate where annual profits ≤ £50,000; BVI Business Company domestic rate 0% (no BVI corporate income tax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: BVI: statutory zero-rating (Economic Substance (Companies and Limited Partnerships) Act 2019). UK (only if UK PE or UK management & control): Full Expensing 100% FYA on qualifying plant/machinery; AIA £1,000,000; R&D tax relief; Patent Box 10%.
